entry.title: A NULL Romance
entry.summary:
I’m a void pointer, no type at all,
I can be anything, but I’m nothing’s call.
I’m looking for meaning, searching for you,
But I don’t even know what I’m supposed to do.

You’re a null pointer, pointing to nothing,
Empty by design, you hold no thing.
We’re both incomplete in our own way,
Trying to find what we’re meant to say.

We drift through memory, nowhere to go,
Two broken pointers, that’s all we know.
If we could connect, if we could align,
Maybe we’d become something that’s fine.

entry.title: The 21 Principles of Dokkōdō
entry.summary:
In the final days of his life, the legendary samurai Miyamoto Musashi wrote down a short but powerful list of life lessons called Dokkōdō, or “The Way of Walking Alone.” These 21 principles reflect a life shaped by discipline, self-awareness, and a deep sense of inner peace. They weren’t meant just for warriors, they’re for anyone looking for clarity and strength in everyday life.

I first came across Musashi while reading the manga Vagabond by Takehiko Inoue, and I was immediately drawn to his character. Watching his transformation, from a wild, almost beast-like swordsman into a calm and thoughtful farmer, left a huge impression on me. That shift felt meaningful, and it made me curious about the real Musashi behind the story.
entry.content:
In the final days of his life, the legendary samurai Miyamoto Musashi wrote down a short but powerful list of life lessons called Dokkōdō, or “The Way of Walking Alone.” These 21 principles reflect a life shaped by discipline, self-awareness, and a deep sense of inner peace. They weren’t meant just for warriors, they’re for anyone looking for clarity and strength in everyday life.

I first came across Musashi while reading the manga Vagabond by Takehiko Inoue, and I was immediately drawn to his character. Watching his transformation, from a wild, almost beast-like swordsman into a calm and thoughtful farmer, left a huge impression on me. That shift felt meaningful, and it made me curious about the real Musashi behind the story.

As I started digging deeper, I came across Dokkōdō. Written just a week before his death, these 21 simple principles capture the core of Musashi’s personal philosophy. They’re honest, straightforward, and surprisingly relevant even today. Reading them, I felt like I was getting a glimpse into the mind of someone who had truly figured out what matters.

The Principles:

  1. Accept everything just the way it is.
  2. Do not seek pleasure for its own sake.
  3. Do not, under any circumstances, depend on a partial feeling.
  4. Think lightly of yourself and deeply of the world.
  5. Be detached from desire your whole life long.
  6. Do not regret what you have done.
  7. Never be jealous.
  8. Never let yourself be saddened by a separation.
  9. Resentment and complaint are appropriate neither for oneself nor others.
  10. Do not let yourself be guided by the feeling of lust or love.
  11. In all things have no preferences.
  12. Be indifferent to where you live.
  13. Do not pursue the taste of good food.
  14. Do not hold on to possessions you no longer need.
  15. Do not act following customary beliefs.
  16. Do not collect weapons or practice with weapons beyond what is useful.
  17. Do not fear death.
  18. Do not seek to possess either goods or fiefs for your old age.
  19. Respect Buddha and the gods without counting on their help.
  20. You may abandon your own body but you must preserve your honor.
  21. Never stray from the Way.

These principles aren’t about cutting yourself off from the world, they’re about living with intention. In a world that’s constantly loud and distracting, Musashi’s words are a reminder to move through life with calm, focus, and a clear sense of purpose.

Follow your own path. Stay true to what matters.

entry.title: My Two Faves
entry.summary:
i strum the strings,
but they don’t sound right.
like my heart when you walk in,
it beats too fast inside.

i practice chords for hours,
trying to get it clean.
but you smile, and i forget,
the song i’ve ever seen.

you don’t care if i mess up,
you laugh, and say, “again!”.
and somehow, with you near,
even wrong notes feel like rain.

i love my guitar,
it’s my old, wooden friend.
but i love you more,
you’re the song without an end.

entry.title: The Simple Path to a Fulfilling Life
entry.summary:
It is not that complicated. It is not easy, but it is simple.

Accept yourself as someone worthwhile. Do not go around feeling like you are not good enough. You are here for a reason, and your job is to figure out where you can make a real contribution.

Take total responsibility for what you are and what you become. That means no blaming others, and no excuses.

Learn to forgive, both yourself and others. Holding on to anger and grudges never built anything good. Let them go.
entry.content:
It is not that complicated. It is not easy, but it is simple.

Accept yourself as someone worthwhile. Do not go around feeling like you are not good enough. You are here for a reason, and your job is to figure out where you can make a real contribution.

Take total responsibility for what you are and what you become. That means no blaming others, and no excuses.

Learn to forgive, both yourself and others. Holding on to anger and grudges never built anything good. Let them go.

Be careful what you feed your mind. Do not waste time on mental junk. Pay attention to the things that help you become a better person.

Set solid goals and work toward them. Know what your values are, and stick to them.

And take care of your body. Everything else depends on it.

entry.title: Coffee
entry.summary:
I’m not really sure why I’m writing this, maybe just to share a thought or two.

“Love is like coffee and sugar. At first, it’s not about the sweetness, but the warmth it brings. Over time, you figure out the perfect mix. It’s not about what’s on the surface, it’s how we just fit together.”

I guess that’s how life works too. We’re drawn to things for the comfort they give, not just the shiny parts. Over time, we realize what truly matters is how something or someone makes us feel, like that first cup of coffee in the morning, or the person who just feels like home.
